analysis.title: Exelon Corp. (EXC): First Take: 3Q beat vs GSe/Consensus; regulatory developments and storage opportunity in focus
key_insights: EXC (Sell) reported 3Q26 operating EPS of $0.87, versus GSe $0.80 and FactSet consensus $0.79. The beat was driven by higher revenue and lower D&A, partly offset by higher purchased power and lower other income.
EXC narrowed 2026 EPS guidance higher to $2.85-$2.91 from $2.81-$2.91, and maintained EPS growth near the top end of its 5%-7% CAGR through 2029.
The high-probability large-load pipeline stayed at ~11 GW. TSA coverage rose to ~45% from ~40% at 2Q, backed by ~$1.2bn of collateral. The future pipeline slipped to ~23 GW from 25 GW.
EXC highlighted a new $3-$7bn storage opportunity beyond the current capital plan. GS is monitoring it, particularly near term in New Jersey.

GS expects investor focus on regulatory developments in Maryland, Illinois and utility-owned generation, on IRAS, RBP and the large-load growth outlook, and on affordability and the policy environment heading into the elections.
GS maintains a Sell rating with a 12-month price target of $44, based on a 14.25x Q5-Q8 P/E multiple. The stock closed at $45.91 on 29 Oct 2026, implying 4.2% downside.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Sell with a $44 target (14.25x Q5-Q8 P/E) after the 3Q26 beat. The stock closed at $45.91, 4.2% above the target.

earnings_insights: EXC 3Q26 operating EPS $0.87 reported vs GSe $0.80 and FactSet consensus $0.79, reported 10/30.
3Q26 revenue $7,319mn actual vs GSe $7,054mn (+$265mn). Purchased power was $2,917mn vs GSe $2,685mn. D&A was $991mn vs GSe $1,095mn. Other, net was $97mn vs GSe $140mn.
2026 EPS guidance narrowed to $2.85-$2.91 from $2.81-$2.91. GSe 2026E EPS is $2.86, with 2027E $3.03 and 2028E $3.23.
GSe quarterly EPS: 6/26 $0.43 (as listed), 9/26E $0.80 (the actual came in at $0.87), 12/26E $0.72, 3/27E $0.97.
risk_factors: Balance sheet cushion relative to the downgrade threshold appealing to investors seeking a defensive name.
Incremental capex opportunities beyond the base level T&D spend.
